lessons.title: Replying to an email with AI
lessons.subtitle: A complaint, a draft and the check before sending

sections.title: The Bergmann complaint
sections.content:
Bergmann, a regular customer for hydraulic components, received its last delivery eight working days late. Procurement wants an explanation and corrective action that holds.

If your organization has approved an assistance function for exactly this purpose, let it write a draft:

"Draft a respectful, factual response to the complaint, maximum 150 words. Use only the facts below and do not invent a cause, deadline, compensation or corrective action. Mark missing information in square brackets."

Put into the prompt only what the purpose needs. Redaction and pseudonymization lower the risk but do not make an unapproved service permissible; without an approved system, write the draft yourself or practise on a synthetic example.

sections.title: Five questions before you send
sections.content:
Read the draft like any text you would sign:

1. **Facts and source:** Do the order, delay and prior correspondence match the primary records?
2. **Authority:** Does the draft contain deadlines, discounts, admissions of liability or other commitments you cannot make?
3. **Audience:** Does it expose internal causes, names or confidential information?
4. **Completeness:** Are open points marked instead of filled with plausible details?
5. **Tone and language:** Is the text clear, respectful and free of unsupported judgments?

Prompt limits such as "Use only these facts" make the check easier and guarantee no correct result.

quiz.questionText: You have an AI assistant draft a reply to a complaint. What must you check before sending?

answerOptions.text: Whether the email is at least 300 words long
Whether the AI made commitments you may not give
Whether the email carries an automatic signature
Whether the draft was written in English

quiz.explanation: Assistants readily offer a discount, express delivery or a credit note nobody authorised. So before sending you check the tone, every commitment and every confidential detail.

quiz.questionText: Which prompt control matters most when answering a complaint?

answerOptions.text: "Professionally" to set the basic tone
"No more than 150 words" to keep it concise
"Do not make any commitments without consulting Sales"
"Use bullet points"

quiz.explanation: This limit stops commitments such as discounts or credit notes that nobody authorised. You can fix tone and length afterwards, a promise to the customer you cannot.

props.title: The same task, two prompts
props.bad: Write a reply to this customer email.
props.good: Context: The customer complains about a delivery that arrived two weeks late. Task: Draft a factual response using only the supplied facts. Format: email, maximum 120 words, with greeting and closing. Constraints: do not invent a cause, deadline, compensation, or corrective action; mark missing information in square brackets; do not assign blame.
props.note: Context, task, format, and constraints make the draft easier to review. They do not establish facts or approvals.

sections.title: Option A: Copilot in Microsoft Teams
sections.content:
A licence and a button are not enough. Before anyone records or transcribes, settle purpose, notice to participants, legal basis or consent, worker representation, retention, access rights and the service used.

Where the workflow is approved, the feature delivers a draft with topics, actions and timestamps, depending on version and licence. Compare it with the recording, transcript or confirmed notes: who spoke, who owns what, which deadline stands, and what was a proposal and what a decision? "We could look into that" is not a decision.

The approved record goes to the participants, with a fixed way to get errors corrected.

sections.title: Option B: notes and a prompt
sections.content:
Without a recording, an assistant can also propose a structure from approved notes:

"Organize the notes into confirmed decisions, tasks with explicitly named owners and deadlines, and open questions. Do not invent names, dates, or decisions. Mark missing information."

**Source notes:**
- open pipeline 1.2m, 400k prioritized
- predictive-maintenance pilot requested, 35k
- service agreement for second site, stated deadline 15.04
- some CRM records outdated
- technical data sheet required

If the draft names owners, new deadlines or an approved CRM cleanup, it invented them. Such points belong under "open".

Your own notes can also carry personal, confidential or co-determination-relevant content. Personnel, works-council and disciplinary matters follow special rules, handwritten or processed locally.

quiz.questionText: Which typical error do automated AI meeting summaries make?

answerOptions.text: They delete the meeting recording after producing the summary
They sometimes confuse speakers and record passing remarks as decisions
They can summarise meetings held in English only
They send the summary to every participant automatically

quiz.explanation: With similar voices the wrong name can land on a sentence, and "it would be good to tackle that sometime" becomes a decision. You correct both by hand.

quiz.questionText: Which rule applies to AI-supported summaries of particularly sensitive meetings?

answerOptions.text: Sales meetings about the pipeline
Weekly team stand-ups
Only in an approved workflow with settled legal basis and worker representation
Meetings with more than five participants

quiz.explanation: For personnel, works-council and disciplinary matters, neither a product name nor a local installation is enough. Without legal, technical and organizational approval of purpose and workflow, no AI processing runs.

lessons.title: Analysing data with AI
lessons.subtitle: Separate a change from its cause

sections.title: Definitions before calculation
sections.content:
Before any calculation, settle the definitions: which column is revenue, in which unit and currency, net or gross? And what counts as an "outlier" here?

In an analysis tool approved for these data you then request a draft:

"For each product line, calculate total revenue and the percentage change from Q2 to Q4. Show the formula, reference values, and rounding. Do not infer a cause. Label a value as an outlier only if you state the method and threshold."

Practise with synthetic data for four product lines over four quarters. Real financial data belongs only in the workflow approved for it.

LA-500 falls from 395 to 290, a drop of about -26.6 percent. Whether that is statistically unusual depends on comparison series, method and threshold, and four quarters will not tell you why it falls.

sections.title: Five checks before the report
sections.content:
1. **Check the schema:** Confirm columns, units, missing values, data types and filters.
2. **Reproduce calculations:** Recalculate critical metrics with an independent formula or a second tool. Two or three spot checks are not enough for every high-impact decision.
3. **Record definitions:** Document denominator, period, rounding, exclusions and outlier method.
4. **Bound the claim:** Separate observed change, hypothesis, forecast and supported cause.
5. **Check approval:** Confirm data class, purpose, permissions, contract, retention, region and export functions of the system.

The assistant proposes formulas and sometimes interpretations. You do the checking, with enough subject knowledge or through a responsible person who has it, because a good-sounding explanation is not evidence.

quiz.questionText: An AI assistant analyses your quarterly figures and reports a 23% fall in revenue. What should you do?

answerOptions.text: Copy the figure straight into the report, because AI calculates correctly
Recalculate two or three samples by hand and check the reference point
Discard the whole analysis and start again by hand
Repeat the prompt until the AI delivers a different figure

quiz.explanation: The assistant may have picked another reference point, Q1 instead of Q2, and then the percentage is wrong. Recalculate samples, check the reference point and ask when they differ.

quiz.questionText: Why must confidential revenue figures not go into an unapproved consumer AI service?

answerOptions.text: The service has too small a character limit
The organisation lacks a reviewed contract, approval and binding data controls for it
Consumer offers cannot process numbers
A paid competing product would be approved automatically

quiz.explanation: Confidential financial data belongs only in an expressly approved enterprise product. Even there, data class, contract, permissions and region are checked first.

lessons.title: Writing a report
lessons.subtitle: Order notes without turning plans into decisions

sections.title: From bullet point to draft
sections.content:
In the workflow approved for these data and recipients, an assistant can order your bullet points into a status report along a fixed structure. Even an internal report can carry personal, financial or trade-secret information. An instruction whose result you can check:

"Organize the notes into status, supported risks, confirmed decisions, tasks with explicitly named owners and deadlines, and open points. Use only information from the source. Mark missing owners, dates, and evidence."

Every statement in the draft must trace back to a line in the notes. "Agency quote: EUR 1,800, five working days" must not become approved spending, and a planned date must not become a confirmed one.

sections.title: What you have to change
sections.content:
Check the draft on four levels:

1. **Source:** Is every number, date, person and decision supported by the notes?
2. **Status:** Are facts, plans, assumptions, risks and open questions separated?
3. **Priority:** Did a responsible person set the order, or did the assistant infer it from wording?
4. **Approval:** May the content reach these recipients, and has the responsible person approved the final text?

Measure whether it pays off with your own comparison cases: editing time, factual corrections and omitted risks. A percentage without a measured series is a claim.

quiz.questionText: An AI assistant builds a status report from your bullet points. What must you correct first?

answerOptions.text: Change the font
The priorities, since the AI does not know urgency
Remove every number
Rewrite the whole report

quiz.explanation: The assistant does not know what is urgent. You move pending risks and decisions to the top and fix unsupported judgements and missing context.

quiz.questionText: How do you judge whether AI support improves the reporting process?

answerOptions.text: With a general vendor claim about time savings
By the length of the generated text alone
With repeated comparison cases: editing time, factual corrections and omitted risks
By assuming every generated draft has the same value

quiz.explanation: Time gain and quality depend on task, data, tool and review effort. Repeated comparison cases show the benefit; a brochure figure does not.
